findings.text: §18's first case says the queued review's dispatch "meets the bound and is queued", then removes "the directory of the dispatch that met the bound" and expects the queued request to launch reading its brief; but a composed run review's brief is composed into the *reviewed* run's directory (materialize_run_review_brief derives the run id from the path's parent and requires it to equal that run's run_dir) and a plan review's brief is copied into the request's own run directory as steering.md, so removing the bound-meeting dispatch's own directory either takes the very copy the deliverable adds — making the case unsatisfiable for a copy stored there — or takes nothing the brief depends on, making the base-revision red arm pass instead of failing with "the brief … is not readable". The Why describes the removed directory as an *earlier refused* dispatch's, so the case and the Why do not name the same directory and the negative control cannot fire as stated

findings.reason: stating a copy as the endpoint leaves the node to discover and resolve a conflict the plan never acknowledges, and the observable the plan actually wants (the request still launches after a directory it does not own is gone) needs no mechanism at all.
findings.text: the deliverable states the endpoint as a mechanism, "a queued request holds a readable copy of its own brief", applied to the three queued composed reviews the Why cites; the queue path (runs._write_steering, reached by queue_dispatch) deliberately leaves a run review's composed brief uncopied, recording that a queue-time copy "would freeze the head it carried then" and that launch re-composes the brief from the reviewed run's record. A copy and a re-composition are different briefs, and the section picks one for a population whose current design forbids it, so a node either freezes the head or deviates from the deliverable

findings.reason: the finding is real but the defect is confirmed by the resolving run and by the reporting session's report, so dropping the dead id costs the plan nothing and changes no decision, and a vanished directory is the very condition the section is about.
